q: What exact DBSCAN eps value and 1%-sample random seed did the paper use for Fig. 3?
basis: The paper's stated 'automatic epsilon search' policy (maximize n_clusters subject to noise<50%) produces 442 micro-clusters on our reproduction, not 5. The paper's Fig. 3 clearly has 5 clusters. This means SCULPT's production algorithm has additional constraints (probably a min-cluster-size floor or a coarser eps lower bound) beyond what the text specifies.
next_steps: Ask authors or inspect SCULPT source for the actual eps auto-selection heuristic; then re-run with published eps + seed to try bit-exact reproduction of Fig. 3 metrics.

q: Why is the released Zenodo dataset ~half the size (953k events) of the paper's stated ~1.9M events, and does that break the paper's claim that 'cluster structure is preserved' under subsampling?
basis: Our replication used the full Zenodo release and still got n_clusters=5 with ARI(cluster, true_state)=0.62 — consistent with the paper. But the Zenodo README does not explain the halving, and it is unclear whether the missing events are randomly held out, filtered by a quality cut, or from a specific state.
next_steps: Run a subsampling-stability sweep at 25%/50%/75%/100% of the Zenodo release to quantify n_clusters, Hopkins, and ARI-vs-truth as functions of sample size; compare against paper's Table if the ~1.9M dataset becomes available.

q: How well-calibrated is the adaptive confidence score against truly bad partitions?
basis: Our re-implementation of Eq. 1 gives 0.87 for a good 5-cluster partition; the paper reports 0.14 for a 'poor separation' partition with only KER/EESum/TotalE (Fig. 7). But the score's tier weights and critical thresholds were empirically tuned on this exact D2O dataset, so overfitting to this single case is possible.
next_steps: Sweep the score over synthetic partitions of increasing corruption (random label permutation fraction 0%..100%) and over other COLTRIMS-like datasets to validate the tier weights and critical thresholds.

q: Which physics features contribute most to cluster-vs-quantum-state correspondence?
basis: Fig. 7 in the paper shows dramatically worse clustering (confidence 0.14) when only KER/EESum/TotalE are used, without alpha_12. Our ablation of KER+EESum+TotalE+alpha_12 gave ARI=0.62; the paper does not decompose this.
next_steps: Systematic feature-ablation: drop each of {KER, EESum, TotalE, alpha_12} separately + add other angular observables (beta angles, azimuthal); quantify marginal contribution to ARI-vs-truth and to the confidence score.

q: Can the ARI-vs-true-state metric (0.617 in our single-shot reproduction) be raised to >=0.9 by the paper's iterative sub-clustering workflow?
basis: The paper claims that iteratively re-running UMAP on lasso-selected sub-clusters isolates all 8 quantum states one-by-one (confidence 0.70 -> 0.79 progression). This is an automatable workflow claim that our batch reproduction could not test.
next_steps: Build a closed-loop reproduction (SCULPT-in-a-Python-loop, not SCULPT-in-a-browser) that recursively sub-clusters until confidence>=0.75 or n<threshold; measure final ARI vs all 8 truth labels; compare against paper's iterative-refinement narrative.
